PullRequest.Title: Disable Uninstall for organization-required plugins
PullRequest.Body: ## Problem In the Agents window, **Customizations > Browse** offers **Uninstall** for a plugin that the organization's managed settings require. Clicking it always fails, and the button becomes **Retry Uninstall**, which can never succeed. Customizations the plugin contributes (prompts, skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers) have the same problem, because their Uninstall removes the whole plugin. Browse didn't check the managed plugin policy the Plugins page already uses. ## Repro 1. Sign in to an account whose organization requires an agent plugin (for example `handy-commands`). 2. Open **Customizations > Browse** and search for the plugin. 3. Click **Uninstall** on the plugin or on one of its prompts. ## What changes Uninstall stays visible but disabled for organization-required plugins and for everything they contribute, with "This plugin is managed by your organization.", the same message as the Plugins page. This covers Browse, the plugin detail, the plugin editor, the Plugins page menu, the section pages' Uninstall Plugin action and the MCP server menu. The reason shows on hover and on keyboard focus with Enter or Space, and is part of the accessible names. Retry Uninstall never appears for these plugins. The plugin detail no longer adds a separate Managed by Organization button for them. Users without plugin policy see no change and no extra rendering. ## Before / After | Before | After (Agents window) | |---|---| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Validated live on Ubuntu 24.04 arm64 with Code OSS built from this branch (`c1f91f4` and `a26cd73`). The org policy came from a local `ChatEnabledPlugins` policy file because the test account's managed-settings refresh returned HTTP 401. Without the policy, the same plugin uninstalls normally. ## Related Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/345128 *🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or search Customizations > Browse while organization-required plugins are installed, including policy changes while results are visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial search still waits on the existing marketplace catalog request; once data is present, the diff adds synchronous required-plugin URI checks while constructing result entries and visible rows. A policyEnablement change triggers render(true), which only rebuilds the local result model and virtualized rows and does not call loadCatalog.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query customization marketplace catalog and browse sources
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one catalog page per query; existing filtered backfill can request up to 8 pages, while browse source sections use existing per-source queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalog and browse-source requests occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold search/browse waits for these existing requests; the changed policy render does not invoke them.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Current search entries: installed customizations plus catalog pages (24 items per normal page, with up to 8 sequential pages only for existing filtered backfill); policy checks scale as entries times the usually small required-plugin URI set. DOM work remains limited by list virtualization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalog pagination and source loading retain their existing sequencing/concurrency. The added derived observable runs synchronously and coalesces equal URI arrays; it starts no asynchronous work and no aggregate burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing marketplace page, browse-section, and installation caches are unchanged. requiredPluginUris is derived/memoized with URI-array equality, so unchanged policy state does not re-render; there is no new positive/negative remote cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing requiredPluginUris, render, renderSearchResults, and loadCatalog: the added observable does not cross a boundary or restart catalog loading.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Organizations may require more than a few plugins and users may have many installed customizations, but the added work is cheap URI comparison/local allocation and visible-row rendering is virtualized.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The local O(entries × required plugins) checks and occasional preserving render are bounded and necessary to update policy state; no expensive boundary is added or moved onto the critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render customization section lists and open inline/context menus for plugin-contributed prompts, skills, agents, or hooks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible row rendering creates the existing context-key overlay and menu; the diff adds one scan of the installed plugin array for rows with pluginUri. Opening a context menu performs the same check once for the selected item.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Row work scales with visible virtualized rows, each scanning installed plugins until the owning URI is found; context-menu work has cardinality one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All added work is synchronous UI-thread CPU work with no queue or asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The installed plugin observable is read directly; no remote cache is involved. No cache lifecycle or retention is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from both added isPluginUriRequiredByPolicy call sites and the helper implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Plugin counts can vary, but practical visible-row and plugin counts keep the URI comparisons bounded; no evidence shows frame-scale pressure.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is bounded local lookup work and does not establish user-visible jank or scaling boundary cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open plugin detail or standalone plugin editor for an organization-required plugin
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action/button is created synchronously; the diff adds a disabled-action view item and delayed-hover registration. Hover content is created only when the button is rendered and no heavy model or boundary work is started.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One uninstall action and at most one hover registration per open detail/editor surface.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous work is started by rendering; hover handling follows the existing hover service lifecycle.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No caches are added or invalidated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed action view item and button render call paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; cardinality is constant per surface.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Constant local UI setup is negligible and correctly disposed with the surface.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Plugins-page or MCP-server menus and attempt uninstall of an organization-required plugin or one of its contributions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Menu creation adds a policy read and disabled tooltip. For required plugins, command guards now stop before confirmation and plugin removal; unmanaged plugins retain the existing confirmation and removal path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove the plugin and its contributed resources
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one removal attempt per user click for unmanaged plugins; zero for organization-required plugins after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, required-plugin actions could reach the existing removal attempt and fail; unmanaged plugin behavior is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing unmanaged uninstall waits for removal. The changed required-plugin path returns before removal, reducing boundary work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One policy check per opened menu/action and one guarded command invocation per user interaction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrent operations are launched. The changed path reduces failed uninstall work for required plugins.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Policy state comes from existing observables; marketplace ownership/removal caches are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the new enabled checks and command guards before remove calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact removal implementation and duration vary by plugin source, but the diff removes rather than adds this work on the affected path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Boundary cardinality is unchanged for unmanaged plugins and reduced to zero for required plugins.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files and all diff pages. Traced discovery rendering, list/menu rendering, detail/editor actions, policy updates, and uninstall call paths. No diff-introduced performance issue met the evidence and impact threshold; no regression-fix record was appropriate because the prevented uninstall is primarily a correctness failure rather than a proven shipped performance regression.
